relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a girl with Blau syndrome carrying a NOD2 variant: "Genetic analysis revealed Met491Leu variant in the NOD2 gene".
method_note: Read by hand; no script transcription of tables (the paper has none besides the CARE checklist supplement, which holds no patient data). Two individuals: the case patient ('patient', rule 5) and a previously published 5-year-old boy mentioned in the Discussion ('ref [9] patient', in scope under v4 because sex, age and features are given); no variant is printed for him, so he has no variants row; the reference title calls him a Colombian child but this was not used for ethnicity because it is only a citation title. Age at last evaluation for the patient recorded as 18-year-old (age at presentation); the text also says she was observed for 2 years afterwards ('In the 2 years we observed') without stating a later age. Age at diagnosis left not reported: the Introduction says she 'has been initially diagnosed with suspected BS for 15 years until her eye symptoms appeared at the age of 18 years', while the Case Presentation says pediatric rheumatologists 'had been unable to give her a definitive diagnosis' after the biopsy at 6 and that ocular symptoms at 18 'led to a preliminary diagnosis of BS'; genetic analysis was at 14 years. This is an internal inconsistency about diagnosis timing. Variant 'Met491Leu' printed without 'p.' prefix; recorded in protein_hgvs_as_stated as printed; variant type not stated by authors (not derived). Authors say 'how it caused the disease is unclear' - not recorded as a pathogenicity classification. 'Sporadic' and 'without any family history' are not parental testing, so inheritance is not reported. Visual impairment checklist left not reported: best-corrected visual acuity 20/20 in both eyes (reduced visual acuity excluded as a feature row under D-27) but she presented with blurred vision; both feature rows emitted. Skin checklist item left not reported: the paper says 'Skin manifestations were not apparent except only roughness located on the trunk and forearms' and elsewhere 'skin lesions'; roughness is not clearly a rash or granulomatous dermatitis. OCT 'No obvious abnormality' recorded as excluded macular abnormality (whole-investigation normal, names only the macula).
